opening.headline: Find out which line of regulations written in the document corresponds to a setting in the administrator console, and identify missing and overdone areas.
body: Although the rule "No work data may be exported to unauthorized external services" is clear to read, there is no setting in the admin console with the same name. Without translations to move the rules into settings, the rules will only be on paper and the controls will be empty.

In this lesson, we'll first look at the locations of settings that administrators can touch in ChatGPT Enterprise and Gemini in Google Workspace, and then walk through matching five lines of rules to settings. Next, you will learn the criteria for judging omissions and excesses, and explain through explanations examples of cases where the prohibition on external sharing applies to various settings.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Regulation sentences can be matched to administrator setting items.
Can determine omissions and excesses of settings

screens.title: One line of regulations, where are the settings?
screens.lead: Read the regulations text on the left and the settings menu on the right side by side. The purpose of this screen is to find what is empty between the two lists.

visual.alt: Illustration of the regulation sentence card on the left and the settings menu list on the right, followed by a question mark dotted line.
labels: Work data should not be sent to unauthorized external services.

paragraphs: One company's information security regulations include this sentence: “Work data should not be sent to unauthorized external services.” When an administrator opens ChatGPT Enterprise's management screen to enforce this policy, menus such as Members, Groups, Permissions & roles, and Plugins are located side by side.

There are no menu names in the prescriptive text, and there are no prescriptive text in the menu. What connects the two is human judgment. If this judgment is not documented, it will have to be reinterpreted from scratch every time the person in charge changes, leaving control empty without anyone knowing that the interpretation has been missed.

In this class, we refer to the task of bridging this gap as regulation-to-setting translation. Translation is not something you do once and is done; it also includes checking whether it complies with regulations every time the settings are changed.

screens.outro: First, let me recall what I experienced while translating.

screens.title: What you missed when moving rules to settings
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't enter or submit your answer, so think for yourself first and then click.

items.prompt: Did I miss anything when moving the rule to Settings?
items.answer: Missing usually means that you have a rule but can't find the corresponding setting, or that you have a setting but haven't turned it on. Both are invisible and are only discovered after an accident. In this lesson, we call this condition omission.

items.prompt: Have you ever complained because the rules were followed but work was blocked?
items.answer: If you push harder than the rules, users will look for workarounds, such as personal accounts or unauthorized tools. Controls may seem strong, but the actual data flow is out of control. This state is called excess.

items.prompt: After changing the settings, have you ever checked again to see if they comply with the regulations?
items.answer: Settings vary slightly as features are added or personnel are replaced. If you do not check against the regulations after making changes, they will become out of sync over time even if you made them correctly at first. Periodic inspection is what makes collation a periodic procedure.

screens.outro: Now that we've figured out all the omissions and excesses, let's check which settings are subject to translation.

screens.title: Settings Map: Where Admins Can Touch
screens.lead: Select each tab to see the settings area where administrators can enforce rules for each provider. It's helpful to pay attention to what you control rather than the name of the realm.

tabs.label: ChatGPT Workspace
tabs.body: ChatGPT Enterprise's Workspace settings are divided into General, Members, Groups, Permissions & roles, etc. General manages the workspace name and AI policy modal, while Members handles member invitation and removal, roles, and seat types. Groups are responsible for creating groups and managing their members, and are especially useful when using role-based access control. Permissions & roles determine which models can be used, access to features such as GPT creation and sharing, canvas, project, memory, and link sharing.

tabs.label: ChatGPT Role (RBAC)
tabs.body: Custom roles determine functional permissions. Each permission is set to Default, On, or Off, and Default follows the workspace settings. Members can have both direct and group roles, and a member can have multiple roles. Only the Workspace Owner can create and assign roles, and it may take up to 5 minutes for changes to be reflected.

tabs.label: ChatGPT plugin
tabs.body: Plugin and marketplace management is done in Plugins in the Admin Console. Plugins can contain skills, apps, and app templates, and installation of plugins and access to apps within them are separate controls. Typically, new plugins and apps are inactive by default and are reviewed and replaced by administrators. Even if a member installs a plugin, he or she cannot use the app-based features unless he or she has access to the included app.

tabs.label: Gemini on Google Workspace
tabs.body: In the Google Admin console, go to Generative AI, Gemini for Workspace, and Feature access to turn Gemini features on and off for services such as Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Docs, Meet, Chat, and Google Workspace Studio. The default is on. You can select an organizational unit (OU) or configuration group to apply to only a subset of users, and group settings take precedence over organizational unit settings.

tabs.label: Claude Help Collection
tabs.body: Claude's collection of security and compliance articles guides you through setup and procedures topic by topic. Data ownership and management, data deletion, organizational data export, data processing when user is removed, custom data retention settings, IP whitelisting, audit logs, and Compliance API are each covered in separate articles. Translation begins with finding which of these items the regulatory sentence corresponds to.

screens.outro: Now that we know where the settings are, let's put the rules into practice.

screens.title: Matching five lines of rules to settings
screens.lead: The table below shows the five lines of regulations and their corresponding settings side by side. Notice which settings each line translates to, and whether more than one setting is needed per line.

visual.alt: An illustration in which the five regulation lines on the left are connected by lines to the setting chip on the right, and the unconnected lines are indicated by dotted lines.
labels: Default disabling and whitelisting of plugins and apps

data.caption: Correspondence table from regulations to settings
rows: The functions that can be used must be different for each role.
Are roles assigned to groups, or are the permissions of multiple roles combined?
Default disabling and whitelisting of plugins and apps (Plugins)
Have you checked installation control and app access control respectively?
Feature access by organizational unit (OU) or group
Do group settings take precedence over organizational unit settings?
Workspace AI policy modal (shown every 30 days)
If I change the policy contents, will it appear again?
Leave a record of who did what
Accumulation from the time it is turned on and retention period
Mark as a missing candidate and find the responsible setting
data.notes: Regulations that do not find a corresponding setting, as in the last line, are missing candidates. Do not delete that line, but leave it in the table so you can fill it in later when you have a corresponding setting. Also, keep in mind that often more than one setting corresponds to a single line.

screens.outro: Now that the correspondence table has been created, let’s look at the criteria for checking the table.

screens.title: Omissions, excesses, regular inspections
screens.lead: The following cards illustrate three criteria for checking the correspondence table. Selecting a card flips it over, and selecting the right arrow moves to the next card.

cards.back: There are regulations, but there are no corresponding settings, or even if there are settings, they are not turned on. The check question is, "Where are the settings and what are their values ​​now that will keep this rule in line?" The empty lines in the correspondence table are the first thing you look at.

Because it is blocked beyond the regulations, work is flowing through detours such as personal accounts. The checking question is, “Does this setting only block as much as the regulations require?” For restrictions that are not in the regulatory text, check whether there are procedures or grounds for exception.

The permissions of ChatGPT's regular custom roles are additive. Even if one role is turned off, members maintain access if the other role allows it. Both direct and group roles are counted, so if you only look at one role, you'll miss out.

cards.front: If only one place is blocked, the remaining path remains.
cards.back: Even if you turn off Drive in Gemini, users can still ask Gemini about Drive files in Gmail. This means that access to the data does not end with turning off one service. You should also check the settings of other services through which your data passes. This card illustrates the typical loophole that arises when regulations are moved to the settings of just one service.

The process of periodically checking the list of roles, groups, and plugins against the regulations. Settings change as functions are added and people change, so even the correspondence table once adjusted may become misaligned over time. Set the inspection cycle and person in charge.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the criteria, let's apply them to cases where a rule spans multiple settings.

screens.title: Explanation: Three settings where ‘prohibit external sharing’ applies
screens.lead: The instructor walks you through the process of moving the no-external sharing rule into settings, layer by layer. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Read the rules
steps.body: The policy is “Do not share work materials outside the organization.” Even though it's just one line, there are multiple ways for the data to go out. Representative paths include those shared directly by users, those that go through connected apps or plug-ins, and those that go through AI functions of other services. Before choosing a setting, list your routes first.

steps.title: Layer 1: User Permissions
steps.body: Restrict sharing and creation capabilities to role permissions in Permissions & roles. Creating and sharing GPTs and sharing links are items in this layer. Because role permissions are combined, ensure that the permission is not permitted in all roles and groups to which the user you want to restrict belongs.

steps.title: 2nd floor: connection path
steps.body: Access to external apps and plugins is blocked or whitelisted in plugin control. New plugins and apps are usually disabled by default, but it's important to remember that plugin installation and app access are separate controls. Blocking the plug-in does not block access to apps that are already turned on.

steps.title: 3rd floor: Service-specific functions
steps.body: Like Gemini in Google Workspace, each service has a separate place to turn it on and off. If organizational unit exceptions and group settings overlap, the group settings take precedence, so make sure no exception departments are inadvertently left open. I also see that Gmail may ask about Drive files even if Drive is turned off.

steps.title: Show remaining detour route
steps.body: Even if you set all three floors, if you only set one floor, the remaining paths remain open. Write all three settings on the corresponding lines of the correspondence table, and if there is an unblocked route on each floor, write it down separately as “remaining route.”

steps.title: Change history and inspection
steps.body: The date and person who changed the settings are recorded in a log for comparison during inspection. Audit logs allow you to track who changed which controls and when, providing a basis for inspection. At every inspection cycle, recheck whether the current values ​​of the three layers match the regulatory sentences.

screens.outro: I will conclude by concluding that one line of regulations can be used for multiple settings.

screens.title: Keep the correspondence table as a living document
screens.lead: We organize the content of this class into one way of working. Read the paragraph below and move on to the final summary.

paragraphs: Moving regulations into settings can be organized into four steps: First, divide the regulatory sentences line by line. Second, find the setting corresponding to each line and write it in the correspondence table. Third, lines that do not have corresponding settings are left as missing candidates, and if there are multiple required settings, they are all written down. Fourth, check for excess to make sure there are no settings that are stronger than specified.

What is most often missed in inspections is that permissions are combined. In ChatGPT, roles and group permissions are added, and in Gemini, even if you turn off one service, a path through other services remains. So, rather than just looking at one setting, you need to look at the combination of all the roles and services the user has.

A correspondence table is not a document you create and end. Settings, people and functions all change, so regular inspections are needed to reevaluate current values ​​and regulations. In some cases, regulations may need to be changed as a result of inspections. Rules that cannot be moved to settings are a reason to rewrite the rules themselves. On the contrary, it is possible to set it, but restrictions that have no basis in the regulations are excessive candidates, so the regulations must be supplemented or the settings must be loosened. The inspection results are left in the response table along with the person in charge, date, and action details, and are used as a starting point for the next inspection.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: One line of regulations can be used to set up multiple settings. If there is only one setting per line in the correspondence table, check again to make sure you haven't missed any paths.

checks.correctFeedback: Each of the four rules has been moved to the appropriate setting.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some regulations were linked to strange settings. Start by distinguishing between what the regulation is intended to control: people, tools, guidance, or records.
checks.explain: A line of qualifications must be moved to at least one corresponding setting; lines without a match are candidates for omission.

checks.intro: Think again from a check perspective about the merging of powers. Just choose the reason that suits you best.
checks.q: ChatGPT's permissions are combined from several roles. Why is it dangerous to just turn off the privileges of one role to block external functions?
options: This is because role permissions take effect 30 days after being turned off.
This is because if you turn off the permission, the audit log will be deleted as well.
This is because users belonging to the group are not affected by any role settings.
This is because if one role is allowed in another role, access is maintained and omissions occur.
checks.correctFeedback: It clearly pointed out the principle that authority increases.
checks.incorrectFeedback: This explanation does not fit with how role permissions are calculated.
checks.explain: Permissions are combined, so if you grant one, access remains. Just like the Gmail route remains when you turn off Drive on Gemini, you miss out on a detour if you only look at one place.

wrong.0: There is no basis for delaying effectiveness and 30 days is the policy modal display cycle.
wrong.1: Changing permissions and deleting logs are unrelated, and changes are logged and used for inspection.
wrong.2: Both groups and roles are affected as they are reflected in the permission calculations.

glossary.def: This is the task of matching regulatory sentences written in a document to specific setting items in the administrator console. If you leave a correspondence table, you can take over even if the person in charge changes.

This is a check that looks for rules that either do not have a corresponding setting or have the setting turned off. In the correspondence table, blank lines and lines with values ​​different from the specifications are eligible.
This is a setting that blocks things more than the regulations require and causes work to flow through detours such as personal accounts.
This is a process of periodically comparing regulations with current settings. Even if settings and personnel change, the correspondence table remains correct.
Role-based access control. ChatGPT divides functional permissions into user-defined roles, and the permissions of multiple roles are added together.

misconceptions.myth: One line of specifications corresponds to one setting.
misconceptions.fact: A single line of specifications usually spans multiple settings, such as role permissions, connected apps and plugins, and service-specific features. Just set one place and the rest of the path is open.

misconceptions.myth: The more you block, the safer you are.
misconceptions.fact: If you restrict it beyond the regulations, users will find detours such as personal tools, and data will move outside of your control. It is safer to block as much as the regulations require and have exception procedures.

misconceptions.myth: If you turn off a service, access to that data is also terminated.
misconceptions.fact: Even if you turn off Drive in Gemini, users may still ask about Drive files in Gmail. You should check together to see if there are any remaining routes through other services.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: One line of regulations is moved to several places in the settings.
Check omissions and excesses together using the correspondence table.
Role permissions are combined, so you see the full combination a user has.
Regular inspections ensure that translations do not deviate.
closing.reflectionLead: The questions below are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Which lines in our organization's regulations have not been mapped to any settings yet? Think of just one candidate setting that will keep you in line.
